messages.author: 994731d36eeef20c
messages.subject: iTRAQ and SILAC analyses
parts:
Dear developers,
first of all, thanks for your efforts in making MSstats available to the community. I've been using it with my shotgun label-free data for some time and am pretty happy with the results.

A while ago I heard (or read) somewhere that you guys were working on a new version to deal with iTRAQ/TMT data. I just wanted to follow up on this one. Can we expect a MSstats version to deal with iTRAQ/TMT experiments? If so, should it be soon or may take some time?
One more thing, can we use MSstats for SILAC experiments as it was a SRM experiment with a reference peptide? In practice I think that it is feasible, however I am not sure whether it is statistically sounding. In other words, I guess that MSstats uses certain statistical assumptions for SRM experiments with SIL peptides that apply to such SRM experiments only and maybe are not applicable to SILAC studies. What is your point of view on this??
Again, thank you for MSstats!
Best regards
Alex

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: iTRAQ and SILAC analyses
parts:
Dear Alex,

Thank you very much for the positive feedback!

For SILAC experiments, where a reference sample is added to every endogenous sample in a constant concentration, MSstats can be used as is. We recommend to look at the profile plots to have a sense of the nature of interferences, and remove run x feature (and possibly condition x feature) interactions if the interferences appear random.

For SILAC experiments where two endogenous samples (e.g. one from each group) are mixed together, MSstats should be applicable in principle. However we haven't had a chance to benchmark it thoroughly, we plan to do this shortly.

For TMT and iTRAQ things are more complicated, since the quantification occurs at the MS2 level, and MS2 spectra create an additional blocking structure. We currently do not account for this in the model. We plan to investigate this in the future, however it will likely to take some time.

I hope that this clarifies things for you somewhat. Thank you again for using MSstats.

Sincerely
Olga
